section.title: Apple Books
section.p: Apple BooksWhen targeting Apple Books (epub.platform=apple), the plugin adds:

ul.li: ibooks:specified-fonts metadata — tells Apple Books to respect embedded fonts rather than using system defaults
ibooks:version metadata — declares the iBooks format version
WebKit-prefixed CSS properties where needed for iOS/macOS rendering

section.p: Apple Books has excellent EPUB 3.3 support and is generally the most standards-compliant major reading system. If your EPUB validates with EPUBCheck and renders well in Apple Books, it will work in most other readers.

section.title: Kobo
section.p: KoboThe Kobo platform (epub.platform=kobo) uses standard EPUB 3.3 with minor CSS adjustments. Kobo readers have good spec compliance and support CSS custom properties, embedded fonts, and ARIA roles.

section.title: Generic (Default)
section.p: The generic platform produces a standards-compliant EPUB 3.3 without any platform-specific modifications. This is the safest choice when distributing to multiple platforms or when you do not know the target reading system.

section.title: Multi-Platform Publishing
section.p: For multi-platform publishingauthors distributing to multiple platforms, the recommended workflow is to build separate EPUBs with platform-specific parameters while sharing the same DITA source:
section.codeblock:
# Generic distribution dita --input=book.ditamap --format=epub3 \ --output=build/generic -Depub.platform=generic
# Amazon KDP dita --input=book.ditamap --format=epub3 \ --output=build/kdp -Depub.platform=kdp \ -Depub.cover.image=cover-kdp.jpg
# Apple Books dita --input=book.ditamap --format=epub3 \ --output=build/apple -Depub.platform=apple
section.p: This single-source, multi-output approach is one of the core strengths of using DITA for publishing.
